From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Olivia Park <olivia.park@blueharbor.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 14 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Exec sign-off required: BlueHarbor MFN / exclusivity / benchmark requests

Olivia / Kenji — thanks for the thorough SOW draft. A few commercial items on their side are high-risk and require deal-desk / exec sign-off before we redline formally:

- Price and discount: they want a 25% committed-volume discount on our inference tier for a 12-month term.
- MFN: they requested an MFN clause guaranteeing price parity with any other inference provider for the same scope.
- Benchmark / parity definition: BlueHarbor inserts a TCO-style benchmark (includes egress + model licensing) with a broad "comparable provider" definition.
- Exclusivity: they ask for a 12-month regional (North America) exclusivity for the segment covered in the SOW.

Attached is the SOW (BlueHarbor_SOW_v1.pdf). Given MFN + broad benchmark + exclusivity this is beyond our standard commercial guardrails and needs leadership review.

Requesting: 1) internal guidance on redlines we can offer, 2) executive sign-off if we should make concessions (specifically for MFN scope/timebox or any exclusivity). I propose we: a) cap exclusivity at 90 days at most, b) narrow MFN to direct equivalent product + exclude marketplace resellers, and c) ask for a performance/binding benchmark process rather than open TCO.

I will hold on sending our counter until I have sign-off.

Thanks,
Tessa
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
attachments: BlueHarbor_SOW_v1.pdf

From: Olivia Park <olivia.park@blueharbor.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Kenji Sato <kenji.sato@blueharbor.com>, BlueHarbor Procurement <procurement@blueharbor.com>
Date: Thu, 14 May 2026 11:08:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Exec sign-off required: BlueHarbor MFN / exclusivity / benchmark requests

Tessa — thanks for sending. A few clarifications from our side:

- Discount: 25% off list for committed monthly inference units over the 12-month contract is a core requirement for us; this is how we justify the consolidation.
- MFN: we need a price-parity MFN that covers any comparable inference offering available to BlueHarbor, including partner marketplaces if offered directly to customers. Our definition of "comparable" is: same model class (transformer-based LLM inference), similar SLA/latency, and equivalent input/output feature set. MFN should include token price + egress and model licensing fees if any.
- Benchmark: if you prefer narrower language, we can accept a clearly defined benchmark process (we'll provide 3 named competitive quotes during negotiation and you commit to match best available) — but MFN is the preferred long-term protection for us.
- Exclusivity: BlueHarbor is requesting exclusivity for the defined segment in North America for 12 months in exchange for a multi-year revenue commitment (we can provide forecast and references).

Can your team confirm whether any of these are deal-breakers? We need to get to a counter so our procurement and legal teams can sign the SOW.

Best,
Olivia
Head of Cloud Partnerships, BlueHarbor Systems

Subject: Re: Fwd: Exec sign-off required: BlueHarbor MFN / exclusivity / benchmark requests

Quick thoughts:

1) Discount — OK to approve 25% for the first 12 months if they commit to the forecasted minimum monthly units and we pin the SOW to that committed volume. Include a step-up/step-down reconciliation mechanism.

2) MFN — propose a narrow MFN: applies only to direct, published token/list price for the same model configuration and identical support/SLA tier. Exclude marketplace-resold offerings and exclude promotional/temporary credits. Timebox MFN to 6 months post-contract signature.

3) Benchmark / TCO — accept a closed-book benchmark process: BlueHarbor must present 3 named vendors and their published commercial terms; we then have 14 days to match materially equivalent public offers. No opaque TCO additions (egress/third-party license fees) unless explicitly listed in the competing quote.

4) Exclusivity — hard no on long-term exclusivity. We can offer a limited "preferred partner" commitment for 90 days (marketing co-sell, priority onboarding) in lieu of exclusivity. If they insist on exclusivity, it requires Rishi-level approval and a material commercial concession (e.g., higher committed volume or pricing steps).

I'm attaching a short redline for the MFN language (redline_mfn_clause.docx). If legal signs off on the language below, I recommend we push this counter to BlueHarbor and offer the 90-day preferred partner + 12-month 25% discount for committed volume.

-Marissa
VP, Enterprise Sales
attachments: redline_mfn_clause.docx

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 14 May 2026 18:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Exec sign-off required: BlueHarbor MFN / exclusivity / benchmark requests

Tessa / Marissa — legal has reviewed Marissa's approach and we can live with that redline with two clarifications to minimize downstream risk:

- MFN clause language (recommended): "Customer will notify Redwood in writing of a materially better published offer for the same product and support tier. Redwood will have 14 days to match the published price. MFN excludes (i) marketplace resales, (ii) promotional credits, and (iii) offers contingent on additional services not in this SOW. MFN obligations shall terminate 6 months after effective date."

- Exclusivity: do not accept any geographic exclusivity across an entire segment for 12 months. If BlueHarbor requires exclusivity, it must be narrowly scoped (named accounts or specific product SKU) and limited to 90 days max. Any exclusivity longer than 90 days requires executive approval and a signed amendment with a defined revenue guarantee.

Given the combination of asks from BlueHarbor, Rishi-level approval is needed only if they push for: (a) MFN without marketplace exclusion, (b) MFN > 6 months, or (c) exclusivity > 90 days.

I drafted suggested counter language in suggested_counter_exclusivity.txt and attached it here.

-Laura
Head of Legal, Redwood Inference

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 15 May 2026 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: ACTION: request for Rishi-level sign-off on BlueHarbor counter approach

Rishi — summarizing the ask and our recommended counter for executive sign-off:

BlueHarbor requests: 25% committed discount (12 months), MFN covering token price + egress + license fees with broad "comparable provider" definition, and 12-month NA exclusivity for the segment in the SOW.

Our recommended counter (need your sign-off to send):
- Approve 25% committed discount for 12 months conditional on committed monthly units and reconciliation.
- Offer MFN limited to direct published pricing for the identical product/configuration and support tier; exclude marketplace resellers and promotional credits; MFN to expire after 6 months.
- Reject broad geographic exclusivity. Offer 90-day "preferred partner" status (marketing + onboarding priority). Exclusivity >90 days requires exec approval and a revenue guarantee amendment.

Attachments: BlueHarbor_SOW_v1.pdf, redline_mfn_clause.docx, suggested_counter_exclusivity.txt

Please reply with APPROVE or DECLINE and any edits by EOD today so I can move the counter back to BlueHarbor. If we get a DECLINE please indicate which of the three items to change.

Thanks,
Tessa
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
